registers.name: RESET
registers.why_reset_value: All 25 resettable blocks come up held in reset at power-on -- the first thing runtime_init() must undo for anything else in this peripheral floor to work.

fields.name: block bit, one per resettable peripheral (see bit_table)
fields.polarity: 1 = peripheral held in reset, 0 = reset deasserted
fields.why: reset_block_num()/unreset_block_num() (resets.h) set/clear these directly. Every peripheral init in the floor -- xosc_init, pll_init (via reset_unreset_block_num_wait_blocking), uart_init's uart_reset/uart_unreset -- touches this first.
fields.source: src/rp2040/hardware_regs/include/hardware/regs/resets.h -- register comment: 'Reset control. If a bit is set it means the peripheral is in reset. 0 means the peripheral's reset is deasserted.' VERIFIED, quoted verbatim.

fields.name: block bit, same layout as RESET
fields.why: Selects which RESET bits the watchdog's reset also asserts. Not on the runtime_init() critical path; included for completeness.

fields.name: block bit, same layout as RESET
fields.why: unreset_block_num_wait_blocking() and reset_unreset_block_num_wait_blocking() both spin `while (~*reset_done & mask) tight_loop_contents();` after clearing the matching RESET bit (src/rp2_common/hardware_resets/include/hardware/resets.h:119-123, fetched this session -- VERIFIED, quoted). pll_init() calls this before touching any PLL register, so RESETS must be correct before PLL_SYS/PLL_USB can come up at all. This is the RESETS.RESET_DONE[n] case the design doc names explicitly as the inverted-polarity example (SS1 point 2) -- CONFIRMED exactly: 'the source polarity is inverted' is precisely what clearing RESET then polling RESET_DONE for the SAME bit to go high does. `when: "clear"` is the correct encoding per the doc's own vocabulary, not a new case.

spin_targets: RESET_DONE -- unreset_block*_wait_blocking() callers spin here. Earliest boot-blocking spin in the whole floor; a stuck emulator hangs on the FIRST peripheral brought out of reset.
